concepts.description: A small ground robot that travels in a straight line and turns in place when it detects an obstacle.

The SRanger controller is composed of a Sensor interface, an Actuator interface, state variables, and a single state machine that selects transitions based on input events, IR distance, and elapsed time.
The SRanger controller has exactly three operating modes: Moving, Turning, and Final.
The SRanger controller defines four real-valued constants used as fixed configuration constants.
The SRanger controller receives input events from three sources.
The SRanger controller emits a single output event carrying two real values for linear and angular velocity.

The Sensor exposes the latest IR distance reading via distance(), returning a real number in metres; when no reading is available it returns a large default value so the obstacle-detection condition is not falsely triggered by missing data.
The Actuator receives Move(lv, av) events from the controller and stores the latest issued command, exposing the last commanded linear and angular velocity for inspection.
The Sensor provides a function that returns the latest IR distance reading; the reading is in metres, non-negative, and is the only sensor measurement consumed by the SRanger controller.
The controller maintains a real variable recording when the controller most recently entered the Turning state.
